title: Brazil’s cultural reach is broad digitally but physical participation remains sharply stratified by education and economic class
source_unit: Observatório Fundação Itaú, Hábitos Culturais 6ª edição, with technical support from Datafolha
geography: Brazil; people aged 16 to 65, with national socioeconomic and education comparisons

observations.period: August 11-26, 2025; cultural participation in the previous 12 months

denominator.unit: people aged 16 to 65 interviewed in person at population-flow locations in Brazil

virtual_participation.unit: percent reporting cultural activities virtually in the previous 12 months

in_person_participation.unit: percent reporting in-person cultural activities in the previous 12 months

basic_education_in_person.unit: percent of respondents with elementary-level education reporting in-person cultural participation

higher_education_in_person.unit: percent of respondents with higher education reporting in-person cultural participation

mechanism.value: Digital cultural reach can be broad while physical attendance remains education-stratified, separating cultural exposure from venue access and social participation

observations.method: Fundação Itaú quantitative survey with technical support from Datafolha; in-person structured interviews at population-flow locations, with a reported maximum margin of error of 2 percentage points at 95% confidence for the total sample.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is self-reported and the in-person flow-location design is not equivalent to a household probability sample. Remote and in-person categories can overlap and do not measure frequency, spending, quality, accessibility, or causal effects of education.
observations.subgroup: People aged 16-65, compared by education and socioeconomic class; the published summary does not provide a full joint education-by-income-by-region table.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher physical participation among highly educated respondents may reflect age, urban residence, income, transport, cultural interest, or survey-location composition rather than education alone. Virtual participation may also require devices, data, privacy, and skills.

observations.period: 2022-2025; socioeconomic class and selected in-person cultural activities

denominator.unit: respondent share within the survey's socioeconomic-class comparisons

class_d_e_in_person.unit: percent of respondents in economic classes D/E reporting in-person cultural participation

class_a_b_in_person.unit: percent of respondents in economic classes A/B reporting in-person cultural participation

cinema_gap.value: approximately 40 percentage points between classes A/B and D/E, stable across the 2022-2025 series

museum_gap.value: approximately 20 percentage points between classes A/B and D/E, stable across the series

theater_gap_change.value: the class gap in theatre access increased from 17 percentage points in 2022 to 28 percentage points in 2025
theater_gap_change.unit: reported change in socioeconomic access gap

mechanism.value: Hybrid cultural access does not erase class inequality: remote participation is more widespread, but physical venues and selected high-cost or place-dependent activities remain unequal

observations.method: Descriptive comparison of the 2022-2025 Fundação Itaú/Datafolha cultural-habits waves as summarized by the 2025 release.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports class comparisons and margins but does not identify whether prices, transport, safety, supply, time, education, or preferences account for the gaps. The series is not a panel of the same respondents.
observations.subgroup: Economic classes A/B and D/E, with activity-specific comparisons for cinema, museums, and theatre.
observations.counterinterpretation: Persistent gaps can reflect unequal urban supply, different age structures, social networks, or willingness to report rather than direct price exclusion; rising gaps in one activity do not establish a general cultural retreat.

related_sources.claim: Complementary 2024 Cultura nas Capitais survey with 19,500 in-person interviews across all Brazilian capitals and the Federal District.
IBGE cultural-indicators context for cultural production, access, labor, prices, and regional infrastructure.

boundary: This record adds a current Brazilian demand-side hybrid-access and socioeconomic-gap layer. It does not establish causal class effects, venue supply, household spending, device or data affordability, cultural quality, or durable participation trajectories.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Fundação Itaú 2025 page reviewed for survey design, sample, virtual and in-person participation, education/class splits, historical activity gaps, and margin-of-error context.
